ideas.description: Exploit. On the E007 recipe (Muon + Lookahead/EMA + progressive resizing 24→28→32 px, 9 epochs), change only the epoch count from 9 to 8.5. Keep the resolution split as fractions of total steps (about 40/30/30%) and stretch the LR and EMA schedules to the new step count. Warm up every resolution in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path. Set torch._dynamo.config.error_on_recompile=True after build so a leak fails loudly. This spends part of E007's 0.60 pp margin and measures the slope with EMA and Muon on.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 4-6%, from 7.33 to about 6.9-7.0 s. Accuracy falls 0.15-0.4 pp to about 0.755-0.757, so the run stays feasible. A drop above 0.5 pp means the EMA+Muon recipe is steeper than H4.2.2 says, and epochs should not be cut further.

ideas.description: Exploit. On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs, change only the end of the LR schedule: decay linearly to exactly 0 instead of 0.07 of peak, for both the Muon group and the SGD groups (BN, whitening bias, head). The warm-up, peak and Lookahead/EMA schedule stay unchanged. This tests whether EMA and a lower final LR are only partly redundant, which the E005 post-mortem predicts.
ideas.expected: Accuracy rises 0.1-0.4 pp (to about 0.760-0.763) with no change in time (±1%). A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.3.4 and buys about 0.5 epoch for the next trim. A gain under 0.1 pp means EMA already captures the low-LR benefit.

ideas.description: Exploit, building on E007's finding that time scales with pixel count. On the E007 recipe at 9 epochs, use a more aggressive resolution schedule: the first 30% of steps at 20 px, then 30% at 24 px, 20% at 28 px, and the last 20% at 32 px. Each resolution is compiled and warmed up in build with channels_last synthetic batches of the exact training shape. Use error_on_recompile after build. Keep the global max-pool head so the network works at every size.
ideas.expected: Time falls 6-10% (to about 6.6-6.9 s). Accuracy falls 0.2-0.5 pp (to about 0.754-0.757). The idea succeeds if the time saved per pp lost is better than the epoch trim's, about 5% per 0.3 pp. A loss above 0.6 pp means 20 px is too coarse for 100 classes.

ideas.description: Exploit. On the E007 recipe, narrow only the last residual group from 576 to 512 channels (the airbench96_faster width). Keep everything else the same, including the Muon lr, epochs and resizing schedule. Re-warm-up all compiled shapes in build.
ideas.expected: Time falls 4-7% (about 0.3-0.5 s). Accuracy changes by -0.1 to -0.4 pp. A loss under 0.3 pp supports H1.5.2 and gives a cheaper per-epoch base that can be stacked with the epoch trim.

ideas.description: Diagnostic, settling the committee's std and 40-seed cruxes (W2, W3). Run the current best recipe (E007, or the 8.5-epoch trim if it is kept) offline on held-out seeds 3-12 with the same harness code path, without editing the recipe. Record per-seed accuracy, the mean, the std and the offset from the seeds 0-2 mean. Also record per-epoch CUDA-event times to settle H3.3.1 (first-epoch overhead) in the same pass.
ideas.expected: The 10-seed mean is within 0.3 pp of the 3-seed mean, and per-seed std is 0.15-0.4 pp. If the 10-seed mean is more than 0.2 pp below the 3-seed mean, the safe margin above 0.753 must rise, which limits further epoch cuts. Epoch 1 is expected to be under 0.3 s slower than later epochs (H3.3.1 refuted).

ideas.description: Explore. On the E007 recipe, capture the train step (forward, backward, Muon Newton-Schulz plus SGD update, and the EMA update on steps where it applies) in CUDA graphs. Use torch.compile mode='max-autotune' (cudagraphs on) or a manual torch.cuda.graph per resolution with static input buffers that the GPU augmentation writes into. Capture every resolution in build on synthetic data. Math stays identical.
ideas.expected: Time falls 2-6% (0.15-0.4 s), because the 4-CPU pin makes launch overhead visible at about 25 steps per epoch with many small optimizer kernels. Per-seed accuracy should be bit-identical or within 0.05 pp. Any recompile or capture inside train shows up as a time rise of more than 1 s and must be checked with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles first.

ideas.description: Explore. On the E007 recipe, after the final EMA/Lookahead weights are copied in at the end of train, reset the BatchNorm running statistics and recompute them with one no-grad forward pass in train mode (momentum=None, cumulative average) over 5k training images at 32 px, inside the timed train. No parameter updates are made, and eval stays a plain forward pass.
ideas.expected: Accuracy rises 0.1-0.4 pp, because the averaged weights no longer match the BN buffers built from the fast weights. The cost is under 0.15 s (about 2%). A gain of 0.3 pp or more supports H1.3.6. Near zero would mean the Lookahead final copy already keeps the BN stats consistent.

structured_output.summary: Best so far: E007 (Muon + Lookahead/EMA + 24→28→32 progressive resizing) at 7.33 s with accuracy 0.7590, which is 0.6 pp above the bar. There are two levers left: spend that margin to cut time, and add accuracy that costs no time. Exploit ideas: trim epochs from 9 to 8.5 (H4.2.2, top priority), decay LR to 0 instead of the 0.07 floor (H1.3.4, adds margin at no cost), a more aggressive 20 px resizing schedule (H2.3), and narrowing the last group to 512 channels (H1.5.2). Explore ideas: a 10-seed held-out run to settle the committee's std and 40-seed-offset cruxes, which also gives per-epoch timing for H3.3.1; CUDA-graph capture under the 4-CPU pin (H2.2.2); and BN recalibration after EMA (H1.3.6). Every compiled change should warm up the exact channels_last shapes in build and set error_on_recompile, to avoid a repeat of E003's leak. All earlier queue entries are already done or dropped, so there is nothing to drop.
